rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām restates the believers’ promised greeting; the Lord gives it through an angel or directly, with direct address heightening their honor.
rows.anchor: بدل من ما يدعون كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers several grammatical parses for qawlan, preferring an accusative specification meaning “I mean,” since the occasion praises this utterance from a merciful Lord.
rows.anchor: والأوجه أن ينتصب قولا على الاختصاص أي : بتقدير أعني

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says God appears to the people of Paradise and greets them; they keep gazing at Him, ignoring every other delight until He veils Himself, leaving His light and blessing with them.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "بينا أهل الجنة في نعيمهم إذ سطع لهم نور

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: The greeting means God has spared His servants burning and separation; mercy gives them strength to hear divine speech and see Him without bewilderment.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" (معنى سلام آنست كه سلمت عبادى من الحرقة والفرقة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The divine greeting is spoken without an intermediary; mercy at that moment grants the vision of God alongside the greeting, completing the bliss.
rows.anchor:
وفي "التأويلات النجمية"
418
يشير إلى أن سلامه تبارك وتعالى كان قولا منه بلا واسطة

rows.speaker: حقائق البقلى
rows.claim: God’s salutation to the truthful is eternal and unbroken in this life and the next; in Paradise every veil is removed from their hearing and sight.
rows.anchor: وفي "حقائق البقلى" سلام الله أزلي إلى الأبد غير منقطع عن عباده الصادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage longs for the Lord’s vision and greeting, then describes God manifesting to the people of Paradise and addressing them with peace.
rows.anchor: فيتجلى الله عز وجل ويقول سلام عليكم يا أهل الجنة فذلك قوله : {سلام قولا من رب رحيم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report maps seven bodily members to seven Paradise rewards: cups to hands, peaceful entry to feet, food and drink to stomachs, eye delight, houris, greeting to ears, and final praise to tongues.
rows.anchor: قيل : سبعة أشياء ثواب لسبعة أعضاء لليد {يتنازعون فيها كأسا} للرجل {ادخلوها بسلام}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is a rebuke spoken to criminals on Judgment Day, between the order to separate and the command to enter Hell.
rows.anchor: من جملة ما يقال لهم يوم القيامة بطرق التقريع والإلزام والتبكيت بين الأمر بالامتياز وبين الأمر بدخول جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is God’s prior instruction about beneficial duties, conveyed through the messengers, including warnings against Satan’s temptation and following his steps.
rows.anchor: والعهد والوصية التقدم بأمر فيه خير ومنفعة والمراد ههنا ما كلفهم الله تعالى على ألسنة الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Children of Adam” here refers to the criminals being addressed.
rows.anchor: والمراد ببني آدم المجرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, “that you not worship Satan” may explain the covenant as a command, or be an infinitive phrase with a preposition omitted.
rows.anchor: إن مفسرة للعهد الذي فيه معنى القول بالأمر والنهي أو مصدرية حذف منها الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping Satan means worshipping anything besides God: no one literally worships Satan, but obeying his prompting resembles worship because both express reverence and because he directs that worship.
rows.anchor: والمراد بعبادة الشيطان عبادة غير الله لأن الشيطان لا يعبده أحد ولم يرد عن أحد أنه عبد الشيطان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Whoever obeys something has worshipped it; Bursevī cites the verse about taking one’s desire as a god as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : من أطاع شيئا عبده دل عليه {أفرءيت من اتخذ إلاهه هوااه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is a manifest enemy because he seeks to divert people from their innate disposition and the service God required of them; this explains why his prohibition is binding.
rows.anchor: يريد أن يصدكم عما جبلتم عليه من الفطرة وكلفتم به من الخدمة وهو تعليل لوجوب الانتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s enmity began with envy after God honored Adam; a rational person should not trust an enemy’s offer, even if it looks beneficial, because it may conceal deceit.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى لما أكرم آدم عليه السلام عاداه إبليس حسدا والعاقل لا يقبل من عدوه وإن كان ما يلقاه إليه خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says humans merit worship of their Creator, who made them for Himself, created other things for them, honored them, and commanded angels and noble servants to bow to Adam.
rows.anchor: لأن مثلكم يستحق لعبادة مثلي فإني أنا العزيز الغفور وإني خلقتكم لنفسي وخلقت المخلوقات لأجلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means worship God alone and associate no one with Him; it is coordinated with the preceding prohibition.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على أن لا تعبدوا وإن فيه كما هي فيه أي : وحدوني بالعبادة ولا تشركوا بها أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prohibition precedes command because purification comes before adornment; the straight path points to worship as monotheism and Islam, and its indefinite form magnifies it.
rows.anchor: وتقديم النهي على الأمر لما أن حق التخلية التقدم على التحلية وليتصل به قوله تعالى : {هاذا صراط مستقيم}

rows.speaker: البقلى
rows.claim: The command calls people to realize the obedience for which they were innately prepared: worship through God, not the ego; servitude never leaves this straight path, and the shahada’s meaning remains true even when unspoken.
rows.anchor: قال البقلى : طلب الحق منهم ما خلق في فطرتهم من استعداد قبول الطاعة

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Worship for one’s own sake is self-worship; worship merely for God’s sake still fails to know Him; true worship recognizes servitude as the jewel of the fitra of lordship.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : من عبد الله لنفسه فإنما يعبد نفسه ومن عبده لأجله فإنه لم يعرف ربه

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Servanthood is marked by abandoning self-assertion, enduring trials, loving the Lord, keeping limits and covenants, and avoiding complaint, sin, and heedlessness in their respective circumstances.
rows.anchor: ومن علامات العبودية ترك الدعوى واحتمال البلوى وحب المولى وحفظ الحدود والوفاء بالعهود

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: True servitude cannot coexist with leadership, since authority contradicts it; the last attachment to leave the hearts of the truthful is love of status.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : لا يصح مع العبودية رياسة أصلا لأنها ضد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God repeatedly advised and warned, criminals ignored His counsel and followed Satan; a sensible person should leave the path of conflict and return to peace.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه كم نصح الله ووعظ وأنذر وحذر ووصل القول وذكر ولكن المجرمين لم يقبلوا النصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dākhir means severe abasement; the phrase describes all resurrected people as humiliated against their will.
rows.anchor: والدخور أشد الصغار والذلة يقال ادخرته فدخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single blast needs no second confirmation; its pronoun may be an explanatory, indefinite pronoun or refer to the resurrection implicit in “yes,” and the sentence can answer an implied condition or explain an implied command.
rows.anchor: لا تحتاج إلى نعم الأخرى وهي إما ضمير مبهم يفسره خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-zajrah is the second blast, named for a shepherd’s cry driving his flock or camels.
rows.anchor: والزجرة الصيحة من زجر الراعي غنمه أو إبله إذا صاح عليها وهي النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden “they” are the polytheists, or, according to some commentaries, all creatures, now alive and standing from their graves.
rows.anchor:
والضمير للمشركين.
وفي بعض التفاسير للخلائق كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Looking” may mean bewildered, seeing as they did before, or waiting to learn what will be done with them.
rows.anchor: حيارى أو يبصرون كما كانوا أو ينتظرون ما يفعل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected cry for ruin to come because this is the day of recompense; the past-tense wording marks the event as certain and present.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الماضي للدلالة على التحقيق والتقرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recognize Judgment Day because they had heard in life that people would be raised, judged, and repaid; the angels call it the day of decisive judgment or of separation between guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: تعليل لدعائهم الويل بطريق الاستئناف أي : اليوم الذي نجازي فيه بأعمالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here gathering means collecting and driving, not resurrection; the wrongdoers are polytheists among Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: الحشر يجيىء بمعنى البعث وبمعنى الجمع والسوق وهو المراد ههنا دون الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their pairs” may mean their counterparts in shirk, disbelief, hypocrisy, and other creeds, grouped with their matching worshippers.
rows.anchor: أشباههم من أهل الشرك والكفر والنفاق والعصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows “their pairs” to mean their wives who shared their religion.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالأزواج نساءهم اللاتي على دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes “their pairs” as their satanic companions, each unbeliever chained with his own devil.
rows.anchor: أو قرناءهم من الشياطين كل كافر مع شيطانه في سلسلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects worshipped besides God include idols and the like; their inclusion intensifies the wrongdoers’ regret and shame.
rows.anchor: من الأصنام ونحوها زيادة في تحسيرهم وتخجيلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the order to guide them includes wrongdoers, their pairs, and their objects of worship; “guiding” them to Hell is sarcastic.
rows.anchor: الضمير للظالمين وأزواجهم ومعبوديهم أي : فعرفوهم طريق جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers can mean anyone who wrongs self or others; each is gathered with those who share or assist the wrongdoing, such as people of wine, adultery, or usury.
rows.anchor: الظالم في الآية عام على من ظلم نفسه وغيره فيحشر كل ظالم مع من كان معينا له

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: In a report from Qūt al-qulūb, a tailor asks whether sewing for oppressors makes him one of their helpers; Ibn al-Mubarak replies that the helpers are those who sell him needle and thread.
rows.anchor: درقوت القلوب آورده كه يكى از عبد الله بن مبارك قدس سره رسيدكه من خياطم

rows.speaker: الفروع
rows.claim: The legal manual says it is disliked for a shoemaker or tailor to take paid work making the dress of immoral people, because this assists sin.
rows.anchor: وفي الفروع ويكره للخفاف والخياط أن يستأجر على عمل من زي الفساق ويأخذ في ذلك أجرا كثيرا لأنه إعانة على المعصية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: A report says that while imprisoned, Abū Ḥanīfa refused an oppressor’s request to sharpen his pen, fearing that he would be counted among their company.
rows.anchor: امام اعظم رضي الله عنه را محبوس كردنديكى از ظلمه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith cited from al-Qurṭubī’s reminder says Imruʾ al-Qays will lead the poets’ banner to Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "امرؤ القيس قائد لواء الشعراء إلى النار"

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: In a dream report, Ibn al-Mubarak says God rebuked and detained him for three years because he once looked kindly at an innovator, asking how the follower of wrongdoers fares after admonition.
rows.anchor: روي ان ابن المبارك رؤي في المنام فقيل له : ما فعل بك ربك؟

rows.speaker: الروضة
rows.claim: Al-Rawḍa says a person of scrupulous piety should decline a sinner’s invitation, and discourages exemplary people from frequenting or publicly honoring people of falsehood.
rows.anchor: وفي "الروضة" : يجيب دعوة الفاسق والورع أن لا يجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exemplary person’s association can make him share the innovator’s blame and help spread false belief and conduct among others.
rows.anchor: وأن يعظم أمره بين الناس فإنه يكون مبتدعا أيضا ويكون سببا لترويج أمره الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People ruled by their commanding selves point others toward Hell through their words, acts, and character, so they are gathered as they died; whoever helps another persist in a lapse shares the punishment and disgrace.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن أرباب النفوس الأمارة كانوا يدلّون في الدنيا على صراط الجحيم من حيث الأسباب من الأقوال والأفعال والأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “detain them” comes from transitive waqqafa, meaning to hold someone, rather than intransitive waqafa, meaning to stand still.
rows.anchor: قفوا أمر من وقفه وقفا بمعنى حبسه لا من وقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passing Sufi aside says egg is lawful and subtle but incomplete until it becomes a chicken; it does not fully satiate, and the broth mentioned is impure.
rows.anchor: البيضة حلال لطيف ولكن أهل التصوف لا يأكلها لأنها ناقصة وإنما كمالها إذا كانت دجاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about turning toward one another is coordinated with the scene of being served drinks: the sincere converse over their wine, as people customarily do while drinking.
rows.anchor: معطوف على يطاف أي : ليشرب عباد الله المخلصون في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise discuss knowledge, spiritual virtues, and what befell them in worldly life among friends and enemies.
rows.anchor: يتساءلون عن الفضائل والمعارف وعما جرى عليهم ولهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense presents these conversations as certain to occur.
rows.anchor: فالتعبير عنهم بصيغة الماضي للتأكيد والدلالة على تحقق الوقوع حتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward reading says even believing monotheists who did not turn wholly to God are people of Paradise; otherwise they would be in the seat of truth with the elect.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن أهل الجنة هم الذين كانوا ممن لم يقبلوا على الله بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion’s question is a reproach for believing in resurrection and accepting that the dead will be raised and repaid.
rows.anchor: طريقة التوبيخ بما كنت عليه من الإيمان والتصديق بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker in Paradise recalls an unnamed worldly companion who mocked his belief in resurrection.
rows.anchor: في تضاعيف محاوراتهم وأثناء مكالماتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madīnūn is the plural of madīn from dīn, recompense, as in the saying “as you do, so you are repaid”; it asks whether they will be raised, held to account, and rewarded or punished.
rows.anchor: جمع مدين من الدين بمعنى الجزاء ومنه كما تدين تدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer asks his companions to look into Hell so he can show them the companion who denied resurrection, thereby proving his account true.
rows.anchor: ناظرون إلى أهل النار لأريكم ذلك القرين المكذب بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His companions tell him to look himself because he knows the man better than they do.
rows.anchor: فقال جلساؤه : أنت أعرف به منا فاطلع أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker sees his companion in the middle of Hell; its center is called sawāʾ because it is equally distant from every side.
rows.anchor: وسمي وسط الشيء سواء لاستواء المسافة منه إلى جميع الجوانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear, fully explicit Book is the Torah, containing the knowledge needed for religious and worldly welfare.
rows.anchor: وهو التوراة فإنه كتاب مشتمل على جميع العلوم التي يحتاج إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustabīn intensifies the sense of clear: the Torah’s completeness makes it as though it explains its rulings and separates lawful from forbidden by its own force.
rows.anchor: فاستبان مبالغة بان بمعنى ظهر ووضح وجعل الكتاب بالغا في بيانه من حيث أنه لكماله في بيان الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical reading treats the added syllables as in yastasḫirūn, making istabāna, tabayyana, and bāna equivalent: the Book simply makes things clear.
rows.anchor: فإن بان واستبان وتبين واحد نحو عجل واستعجل وتعجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided Moses and Aaron through the Book to the straight path leading to truth and right judgment, through its detailed laws and rulings.
rows.anchor: الموصل إلى الحق والصواب بما فيه من تفاصيل الشرائع وتفاريع الأحكام

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: The straight path means Islam, and God established the two prophets in it; the road image is transferred to the true religion in a verified metaphor.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : وهديناهما دين الله الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward reading takes their guidance as the gift of true knowledge and divine inspirations leading to the presence of the One and the Unique.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى إيتاء العلوم الحقيقية والإلهامات الربانية والهداية بذلك إلى الحضرة الواحدية والأحدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserved Moses and Aaron’s good name among later peoples, who continue to invoke peace upon them and pray for them through the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: أبقينا عليهما فيما بين الأمم الآخرين هذا الذكر الجميل والثناء الجزيل فهم يسلمون عليهما يقولون سلام على موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives complete, fitting recompense to benefactors; Moses and Aaron are among the believing servants, and faith is the unseen’s station while ihsan is the station of direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن طريق الإحسان هو الإيمان فالإيمان هو مرتبة الغيب والإحسان هو مرتبة المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since faith arises from knowledge, knowing God and acting on that knowledge are humanity’s foundation; human distinction lies in speech, knowledge, understanding, and other perfections, beyond plant, animal, or mere bodily form.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإيمان ينشأ عن المعرفة كان الأصل معرفة الله والجري على مقتضى العلم فالإنسان من حيث ما يتغذى نبات

rows.speaker: البرهان
rows.claim: Al-Burhān notes that the second pronoun is omitted, relying on the first for the sense.
rows.anchor: وفي "البرهان" حذف الضمير من الثاني اكتفاء بالأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet; “Lord of Might” apposes “your Lord,” and the verse tells him to declare God beyond the attributes polytheists falsely assign, including children, spouses, and partners.
rows.anchor: خطاب للنبي عليه السلام وقوله : {رب العزة} بدل من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their false descriptions include claiming that God has abandoned His support of the Prophet, as their demands for punishment imply.
rows.anchor: من الأولاد والأزواج والشركاء وغير ذلك من الأشياء التي من جملتها ترك نصرتك عليهم كما يدل عليه استعجالهم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: “Lord of Might” either indicates that might belongs exclusively and intrinsically to God, or that created might belongs to those He ennobles; even created might remains His property, placed where He wills.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : أضاف الرب إلى العزة لاختصاصه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines negation and relational attributes: “Glory” negates defects, while “Lord of Might” indicates positive relations; the parallel is “Lord of Majesty and Honor.”
rows.anchor: وفيه إشعار بالسلوب والإضافات كما في قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation comes before positive relation because God’s essence needs no other, while a relation exists only when both related parties exist.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم السلب على الإضافة لأن السلوب كافية فيها ذاته من حيث هو هو بخلاف الإضافات

rows.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Subḥān Allāh negates every defect from God’s essence and attributes; names of negation, such as the Holy and the Peace, fall under it.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام سبحان الله كلمة مشتملة على سلب النقص والعيب عن ذات الله وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are intermediaries between God and His servants; salutation to them signals their high rank and their safety, deliverance, and attainment of every aim.
rows.anchor: ثم إن المرسلين لما كانوا وسائط بين الله وبين عباده نبه على علو شأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers convey God’s messages and explain religious and worldly needs; naming Adam first and Muhammad last, the verse extends the greeting to all after particular messengers were named.
rows.anchor: الذين يبلغون رسالات الله إلى الأمم ويبينون لهم ما يحتاجون إليه من الأمور الدينية والدنيوية أولهم آدم وآخرهم محمد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says that those greeting the Prophet should also greet the messengers, since he is one of them; another says to make blessings upon him general, including his family and companions.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إذا سلمتم علي فسلموا على المرسلين فإنما أنا أحدهم"

rows.speaker: المقاصد الحسنة
rows.claim: Al-Maqāṣid al-ḥasana says it did not find the first hadith in this exact wording; its possible meaning is to bless the Prophet along with God’s other prophets, whom God sent as He sent him.
rows.anchor: قال في "المقاصد الحسنة" : لم أقف عليه بهذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: عز الدين
rows.claim: Al-ʿIzz says praise affirms every kind of perfection in God’s essence and attributes; names such as All-Knowing, Powerful, Hearing, and Seeing are included in it.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : الحمدكلمة مشتملة على إثبات ضروب الكمال لذاته وصفاته

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd reads the closing praise as affirming positive attributes after God’s negative attributes, and as showing that these entail His beautiful acts and the gifts and worldly and religious perfections bestowed on prophets and followers.
rows.anchor: قال المولى أبو السعود : هذا إشارة إلى وصفه تعالى بصفاته الكريمة الثبوتية

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: The ending signals that the promised victory and supremacy have come to pass.
rows.anchor: وإشعار بأن ما وعده من النصرة والغلبة قد تحقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing teaches believers to glorify and praise God and greet His messengers, whose mediation brings religious and worldly perfections; their divinely enabled role is itself a favor deserving praise.
rows.anchor: والمراد تنبيه المؤمنين على كيفية تسبيحه وتحميده والتسليم على رسله الذين هم وسائط بينهم وبينه عز وجل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say God is praised for destroying unbelievers and saving believers, and in every circumstance, whether pleasant or painful, beneficial or harmful.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : والحمدعلى إهلاك الكافرين وإنجاء المؤمنين وعلى كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one soul is Adam; Eve was made either from Adam’s kind or from his short rib, identified as the rib near the flank or the last rib. The omitted clause avoids implying that Eve was created after Adam’s offspring.
rows.anchor: وهي الضلع التي تلي الخاصرة ، أو هي آخر الأضلاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inward reading takes the single soul as the spirit and its spouse as the heart, created from it as Eve was from Adam’s rib; God alone creates, so He should be worshipped without association.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى خلق الإنسان من نفس واحدة هي الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sent down” may mean decreed and apportioned, written in the Preserved Tablet, or brought about through heavenly causes such as rain and starlight.
rows.anchor: أي : قضى وقسم لكم ، فإن قضاياه تعالى وقسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with the clothing verse, God sends the water that produces cotton and wool rather than the clothing itself.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله : قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا ، ولم ينزل اللباس نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight livestock pairs are male and female camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; anʿām originally denotes a group of camels and has no singular of that form.
rows.anchor: ذكرا وأنثى ، هي الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز والأنعام جمع نعم

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh restricts anʿām to four kinds, yielding eight pairs because each species’ male and female form a pair; horses, mules, and donkeys are excluded.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في أول المائدة : الأنعام مخصوص بالأنواع الأربعة

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr explains that each of two things of the same kind is a pair, while in arithmetic “even” contrasts with “odd.”
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" الواحد إذا كان وحده ، فهو فرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These four animal types are singled out because people benefit from their meat, hides, hair, and wool.
rows.anchor: وخصصت هذه الأنواع الأربعة بالذكر لكثرة الانتفاع بها من اللحم والجلد والشعر والوبر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: An inward reading interprets the eight livestock pairs as eight animal traits in humans: eating, drinking, excretion, urination, desire, greed, rapacity, and anger.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The traits reduce to desire and anger, which every animal needs to survive: desire attracts benefits, and anger repels harms.
rows.anchor: وأصل جميع هذه الصفات الصفتان الاثنتان : الشهوة والغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ummahāt means mothers and adds hāʾ to umm, as ahraqa adds hāʾ to araqa.
rows.anchor: أي : في أرحامهن جمع أم زيدت الهاء فيه كما زيدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation proceeds in stages: a living, proportioned being develops from bones covered with flesh, bare bones, formed and unformed mors, a clot, and a drop of semen.
rows.anchor: أي : خلقا مدرجا حيوانا سويا من بعد عظام مكسوة لحما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta, the thin membrane surrounding the fetus; another account lists the loins, abdomen, and womb.
rows.anchor: وهي ظلمة البطن وظلمة الرحم وظلمة المشيمة ، وهي بالفتح محل الولد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: An inward reading calls the three darknesses the darkness of created nature, of the spirit’s existence, and of human nature, or body, nature, and self.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى ظلمة الخلقية وظلمة وجود الروح وظلمة البشرية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: As a fetus emerges at birth from physical darkness into the visible world, the spiritual seeker’s second birth leads from these darknesses into the unseen world of the heart and spirit.
rows.anchor: فكما أن الجنين يخرج في الولادة الأولى من الظلمات المذكورة إلى نور عالم الملك والشهادة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafez’s couplet urges the soul to spread its wings and call from the Tree of Ṭūbā rather than remain imprisoned in its cage.
rows.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
بال بكشا وصفير از شجر طوبى زن
